[990] Austrian security and defense doctrine

[991] On December 12, 2001, the National Council, with the votes of the governing parties ÖVP and FPÖ, adopted a new security and defense doctrine that took into account the paradigm shift in security policy after

[992] As early as November 16, 2001, the establishment of a National Security Council (NSC) was decreed by law in a broad national consensus

[993] These two events brought about substantial changes in both the conception and the structure for dealing with security policy-relevant issues

[994] The creation of the new doctrine was intended to take account of security policy developments

[995] In this endeavour, it follows three guidelines

[996] Austrian security policy is based on the principle of comprehensive security. The first part of the security and defense doctrine represents a concentration of the analysis section, the draft of which was prepared by a commission of experts in 2000 and submitted to the National Council for parliamentary consideration on January

[997] This section of the analysis forms the basis for the “General Considerations” and presents the security policy paradigm shift in Europe after 1989 and the Austrian security situation as well as Austria’s integration and solidarity-based participation in international organizations

[998] Concrete guidelines for the design of security and defence policy are set out in the second part of the doctrine, the resolution of the National Council, as “recommendations”

[999] The nine general recommendations for shaping security and defense policy particularly emphasize the crucial importance of involving society through comprehensive and ongoing information, as well as the need to establish and expand security policy research expertise

[1000] The explicit mention of securing vital resources and protecting strategic infrastructure represents a certain novelty in this area and, in light of developments since 1989, is groundbreaking for future challenges

[1001] A clear commitment to active and solidarity-based participation in the common European security and defense policy and its further development can be found in the 14 “foreign policy aspects”

[1002] Regarding the design of defence policy, which gives appropriate importance to both the military and non-military aspects of security

[1003] The principle of preventive security replaces the threat response concept

[1004] Active participation in international conflict prevention and crisis management measures is an important component of Austria's security policy

[1005] The principle of European solidarity replaces the concept of an autonomous security policy

[1006] The security of Austria and the EU are inextricably linked

[1007] The new security policy challenges and risks cannot be addressed alone, but only through international cooperation based on solidarity

[1008] a corresponding basic order and a resulting quantity structure can be derived

[1009] Essentially, this can be based on two pillars – the protection and defense of Austria and its population, and the contribution to international peacekeeping missions, particularly within the framework of the European Union

[1010] The principles according to which Austria's internal security policy is to be shaped primarily emphasize democratic and constitutional aspects

[1011] They are primarily focused on combating international terrorism and organized crime, as well as participating in the EU's civilian crisis management

[1012] With the adoption of the doctrine on 12 December 2001, only one of several steps was taken

[1013] At the end of the resolution, the National Council requests the Federal Government to develop partial strategies for all areas relevant to security policy on the basis of the recommendations presented

[1014] These should include, in particular, the measures necessary to implement the recommendations

[1015] In addition to the areas of foreign and defense policy and internal security already mentioned in the doctrine, substrategies for economic, agricultural, infrastructure, financial, education and information policy are also to be developed

[1016] With the adoption of the overall and partial strategies, the third phase of the doctrine process would be completed

[1017] This would also create the material prerequisite for replacing the “National Defence Plan” (LV-Plan) adopted by the then Federal Government in

[1018] National Security Council

[1019] On November 17, 2001, the Federal Law on the Establishment of a National Security Council (NSC) came into force

[1020] Based on the experience of political practice, it has become apparent that issues of Austrian foreign, security and defense policy as well as integration policy have so far been dealt with in parallel in various advisory bodies of the Federal Government, in the so-called EU Main Committee of the National Council and in the Federal Council

[1021] In order to streamline and increase efficiency, it was decided to merge the Foreign Affairs Council and the National Defence Council into a single advisory body (NSR

[1022] As a current background, the attacks in New York and Washington in 2001 and, in particular, the subsequent concerted measures to combat international terrorism have confirmed the indispensable need for an efficient and unified platform for relevant consultations

[1023] The newly created NSR – in line with the tasks of the previous bodies – performs advisory tasks for the Federal Government and also issues relevant recommendations

[1024] Furthermore, the NSR is intended to contribute to improving the cooperation of the parties represented in the National Council in the field of foreign, security and defense policy and to develop the basis for decision-making for the responsible bodies of the state

[1025] The National Security Council is established as an independent collegial body at the level of the highest executive bodies at the Federal Chancellery and covers the areas of responsibility of the Council for Foreign Affairs and the National Defence Council

[1026] The primary task of the Council is to advise the Federal Government and the individual Federal Ministers on all fundamental matters of foreign, security and defence policy

[1027] This includes, among other things, matters for which the National Defense Council was previously responsible

[1028] matters of military national defense which are of fundamental importance and go beyond the competence of the Federal Minister of Defense, hearings before the Federal Government makes a decision, but in any case before the Federal President submits a proposal to the Federal President for the call-up of conscripts for operational presence service or deferred presence service, unless there is imminent danger, and hearings before the Federal Minister of Defense orders the call-up of conscripts for operational presence service or deferred presence service or for extraordinary exercises, unless there is imminent danger

[1029] Furthermore, the Council must be consulted on matters relating to the EU's Common Foreign and Security Policy pursuant to Article 23f paragraph 3 of the Federal Constitutional Law (so-called Petersberg tasks) and on matters falling within Chapter VII of the United Nations Charter (measures in the event of threats to the peace, breaches of the peace and acts of aggression

[1030] In addition, members of the government who are members of the Council, as well as representatives of the political parties, may make issues which they consider to be of fundamental importance the subject of the discussions, i.e. the Council must be consulted on any other matter of foreign, security and defence policy if a voting member so requests

[1031] Composition The NSR consists of the Federal Chancellor as Chairman, the Vice Chancellor, the Federal Minister for Foreign Affairs, the Federal Minister of Defence, the Federal Minister of the Interior and the Federal Minister of Justice as well as 11 representatives of the parties represented in the Main Committee of the National Council according to their mandate strength (both National Council members and Federal Council members) as permanent voting members

[1032] In addition, the Council shall include an official from the Presidential Chancellery, a representative of the Chairman of the Conference of State Governors, the Secretary General for Foreign Affairs, the Chief of the General Staff, the Director General for Public Security, and one further qualified minister appointed by the Federal Chancellor, the Vice Chancellor, the Federal Minister for Foreign Affairs, and the Federal Minister of Defence in an advisory capacity

[1033] In addition, other relevant federal ministers or state secretaries must be consulted, as well as state governors or other experts if necessary

[1034] Normally, the Council meets at least every six months

[1035] However, any voting member of the Council may at any time request that the Federal Chancellor convene the Council within days

[1036] European Security Strategy (ESS

[1037] The European dissonances during the Iraq crisis have shown that a coherent foreign and security policy can only be successful if it is based on a common strategic concept

[1038] In June 2003, the High Representative for the Common Foreign and Security Policy, Javier Solana, presented the draft text of the European Security Strategy, which was then adopted by the European Council on 12 December

[1039] The EU strategy is divided into three interrelated and mutually influential chapters: The first part, "New threats in a new security environment," deals with the security environment: global challenges and main threats with the components of terrorism, proliferation of weapons of mass destruction and their delivery systems, regional conflicts, failed states, and organized transnational crime

[1040] The second chapter covers the “Strategic Objectives” and points out right at the beginning that the new threats are "dynamic in nature” and “the first line of defense will often be abroad

[1041] In contrast to the USA, the EU focuses on conflict prevention and threat prevention

[1042] Because, in contrast to the Cold War, there are no longer purely military threats, “a mixture of intelligence, police, legal, military and other White Paper 2004 Analysis Balance Perspectives means” may be appropriate in the fight against terrorism, for example

[1043] At the level of international law, the EU is committed to strengthening the multilateral system and advocates efficient multilateralism

[1044] For the EU, the transatlantic relationship is one of the “fundamental elements of the international system”

[1045] The EU does not want to compete with NATO, but rather strengthen the European pillar of this organization

[1046] The third chapter of the paper deals with the ‘Impact on European Policy’

[1047] For the EU, it is of great importance to develop a "strategic culture" that promotes early, rapid and, if necessary, robust action

[1048] In addition, the transformation of the armed forces into flexible, rapidly deployable mobile forces is essential

[1049] For the EU, the use of military force is always a last resort

[1050] Before that, all means of preventive diplomacy would have to be exhausted

[1051] In addition to strengthening civilian crisis management capacities and diplomatic capabilities, the strategic partnership between the EU and NATO should be expanded and greater importance given to the strategic partnership with Russia

[1052] Strategic partnerships with Japan, China, India and Canada are also to be developed

[1053] With the adoption of the Security Strategy, the EU has achieved a new quality of security policy thinking by conducting a common threat analysis and drawing common conclusions from it

[1054] It is essential for the credibility of the EU that the ESS is implemented gradually

[1055] Comparison between the USA and the EU

[1056] The US National Security Strategy (NSS) is a comprehensive national strategy including clear implementation concepts, while the EU strategy is a supranational declaration of intent whose implementation provisions remain open

[1057] When assessing the threat situation, both strategies are almost identical

[1058] Both aim at an active defense policy, although the means and methods differ

[1059] The NSS believes that the “best defense is a good offense” and reserves the right to preemptive interventions (“preemptive strikes”

[1060] The US – in contrast to the EU – is willing to act outside multilateral structures if necessary

[1061] While the US strategy is based on a global perspective and precisely such security interests, Europe is strongly continental-regionally centered and has its interests in its immediate neighborhood

[1094] Austria's military system

[1095] General The basis for the establishment of an army is the military system

[1096] A distinction must be made here according to two criteria

[1097] Firstly, the manner in which staff are provided and supplemented, i.e., the recruitment of personnel

[1098] Here, one can distinguish between the basic patterns of general conscription, selective conscription and voluntary recruitment of personnel (professional army, volunteer army, “Foreign Legion”

[1099] A second criterion is the manner of “creating the operational organization,” i.e. how this organization – the operational army – is formed

[1100] Here, a distinction can be made between the presence system (the “standing army” or “presence army”), the cadre framework organization, and the militia system

[1101] In many respects, mixed forms (such as a volunteer army supplemented by militia soldiers when necessary) emerge, since the military and organizational forms mentioned above are ideal-typical systems

[1102] The following briefly describes the systems and possibilities for the provision of information: 58 Conscription Army

[1103] The recruitment and supplementation of the troops takes place on the basis of general conscription, in Austria restricted to the male population, while the cadre positions are usually filled by professional or temporary soldiers

[1104] However, various reasons for exclusion – social conditions (e.g. length of civilian service) or unfitness – limit the availability of conscripts

[1105] Selective conscription: This is characterized by a high degree of exceptional cases (such as the White Paper 2004 Analysis Balance Sheet Perspectives University Studies) which result in exemption from conscription

[1106] General service obligation (community service): service obligation that extends to both military service and civilian service (civil protection, rescue service, care for the disabled and elderly, relief service abroad

[1107] Allocation to the service types is based on voluntary notification and in accordance with the availability of duty stations

[1108] Militia system: Army organization that focuses primarily on the training and equipment of personnel and has no or only a few operational units in peacetime

[1109] Depending on the peacekeeping structure, active cadre personnel are designated to perform specific functions in the operational units

[1110] These units are replenished by militia soldiers as part of a full or partial mobilization

[1111] Cadre militia: Army organizations that provide a relatively large cadre of active leadership personnel for future operational units

[1112] Cadre framework army: Organization whose intended operational units already have the full leadership and functional personnel, i.e. the “framework,” in peacetime, and which are filled up to their required strength by trained reservists in the event of an operation

[1113] Volunteer army/professional army: Personnel are provided exclusively by volunteer soldiers who serve for a specific period of time

[1114] If they are employed until their retirement or until they become unfit for service, they are professional soldiers

[1115] Temporary soldiers serve for a limited period of time based on their contract and, depending on the contract, may subsequently be available for functions in the militia/reserve during troop exercises or mobilization

[1116] Recently, there has been a trend towards volunteer armies in Europe

[1117] Standing Army (Presence Army

[1118] Armed forces that are trained, structured and equipped for deployment in peacetime and that are available at short notice without mobilisation

[1119] It is of secondary importance whether personnel are recruited by volunteers or conscripts, or by both; what is more important is the objective of having sufficient armed forces in peacetime, measured against the threat

[1120] Principles of the militia system Militia is used to describe armed forces which – in contrast to standing armies – are called up only for training purposes and for specific operational situations

[1121] The following characteristics are ideal

[1122] A tendency to recruit as fully as possible all those fit for military service to perform the defense tasks of a community; a time commitment in the form of a relatively short initial training period followed by short periods of secondary training

[1123] the planning and implementation of training and deployment of the militia under the greatest possible responsibility of militia members

[1124] the recognizable presence of the militia army even in times of relative peace; the highest possible acceptance of the militia army among the general population

[1125] The militia system means that the operational organization is largely carried out by conscripts from the militia, who are deployed when necessary for tasks that exceed the capacity of the present forces

[1126] In peacetime, the militia system has no or only a few operational units

[1127] The focus is primarily on the training of the enlisted personnel, but also of officers and non-commissioned officers

[1128] It depends on the respective peace organization to what extent active leadership personnel are already designated in peacetime for use in certain positions in the future operational units, which will be filled with militia soldiers

[1129] If a relatively large active cadre is available for the future associations, the system of the "cadre militia" is approached

[1130] The few operational units already existing in peacetime are usually set up for training purposes or as standby troops, while the bulk of the personnel are only called upon after mobilization

[1131] If the recruitment of militia soldiers is based primarily on volunteers who have committed themselves to a longer service in the reserve organization, one can speak of a “volunteer militia.”

[1132] If the militia personnel are deployed according to the territorial principle, ie the militia soldiers are trained near their hometown if necessary and are also integrated into operational units close to their hometown, this is also referred to as a "territorial militia

[1436] Establishment according to the principles of a militia system Applicable law: Article

[1437] The Federal Army is responsible for national military defense

[1438] It shall be established according to the principles of a militia system

[1439] According to Article 79 paragraph 1 of the Federal Constitutional Law (B-VG) as amended by the Federal Law Gazette (BGBl

[1440] No. 341/1988, with effect from 1 July 1988, “the Federal Army is to be established according to the principles of a militia system”

[1441] Thus, the militia-like organizational structure of the Federal Army – a larger army with a militia-like character and the maintenance of permanently present units – is constitutionally anchored

[1442] The ordinary military law legislator is bound to this organizational form of military national defense

[1443] When establishing the militia system in 1988, the constitutional legislator assumed the following three main components of the Austrian militia system: — a comparatively short period of basic military service plus periodic repetition exercises spread over a longer period, — the design of the protection and defense task (at least predominantly) not through a professional institution, but as a community task, — the existence of a specific, comparatively small portion of a "standing army" to ensure rapid reaction capability in the event of an emergency

[1444] These three cornerstones are therefore constitutionally prescribed and are not at the discretion of either the legislature or the executive

[1515] Military Powers Act, Neutrality, Supreme Command 6.1.5.1 Military Powers Act (MBG

[1516] The MBG, which came into force on 1 July 2001, standardises the powers of military authorities and bodies and also regulates the specific legal protection institutions for the military sector

[1517] This law consolidated fundamental tasks and powers that had previously existed as individual provisions in various laws and regulations and supplemented them with new provisions

[1518] The special tasks and powers regulated in Part 2 of the Act include security services, military intelligence services and airspace surveillance

[1519] Another part of the law deals with the right of the Federal Army to make use of material and work services for the purposes of military national defence, insofar as they are essential for the fulfilment of operational tasks

[1520] White Paper 2004 Analysis Balance Sheet

[1521] The legal protection of citizens with regard to compensation for damages that may arise from the exercise of powers by military bodies is also regulated

[1522] This part of the law concerns indemnification, a right of appeal, and the installation of independent legal protection officers to exercise legal control over the intelligence services

[1523] Federal Constitutional Law on the Neutrality of Austria With the Federal Constitutional Law of 26 October 1955, on the neutrality of Austria, Austria declared its "perpetual neutrality of its own free will

[1524] This Federal Constitutional Law was sent to the states existing at that time for their information

[1525] By enshrining permanent neutrality in an Austrian legal act, it is made clear that the determination of neutrality status is a matter solely for Austria

[1526] It is particularly noted that under Austrian law (Section 320 of the Criminal Code), the prohibited support of parties to armed conflicts (formerly known as "endangering neutrality") is punishable by imprisonment from six months to five years

[1527] With the dissolution of the Warsaw Pact and the end of the political-ideological East-West conflict, neutrality has lost much of its foreign policy significance; greater emphasis has been placed on the duty of international solidarity (see above

[1528] The political developments just mentioned resolved, at least temporarily, the mutual blockade of the permanent members of the UN Security Council, which, from the Austrian perspective, led to legal tensions between strict adherence to neutrality and participation in UN sanctions measures

[1529] Together with the moral requirement not to stand aside in a commitment against an aggressor, there was a change in the concept of neutrality in the sense of a willingness to show international solidarity

[1530] Permanent neutrality is not mentioned in the EU accession treaty

[1531] Since unilateral economic sanctions are also adopted within the framework of the CFSP, which is hardly compatible with the traditional understanding of neutrality, Austria has expressly decided in Article 23f of the Federal Constitutional Law to participate comprehensively in the CFSP, including the imposition of unilateral economic sanctions against third countries

[1532] Due to an amendment to the Federal Constitutional Law, Austria can also participate in further efforts towards a common European Security and Defence Policy (ESDP

[1533] According to this, decisions of the European Council on a common defence of the EU and on the integration of the Western European Union into the EU require prior approval by the National Council and the Federal Council and may only be implemented with a two-thirds majority

[1534] Current legal situation (Federal Constitutional Law on the Neutrality of Austria): Article I

[1633] The Road to the Federal Army 2004 Preliminary Remarks

[1634] The Austrian Armed Forces are currently undergoing the most substantial changes in their almost fifty-year history

[1635] After Austria regained its independence, a small army was created “in the storm of difficult times,” which had to pass its first test in

[1636] For decades, this army was characterized by the territorially oriented defense strategy of a small neutral state, which increasingly lost importance from 1989 onwards with the end of the post-war order

[1637] After almost 15 years of changing reforms, the Austrian armed forces are now presenting their new profile in the light of the Federal Army Reform Commission

[1638] All these changes are a mandate and reason enough to present the current status, requirements and development prospects of the armed forces in the 2004 White Paper, based on a historical review

[1639] Development of the Federal Army

[1640] From the State Treaty of 1955 to the geopolitical turning point of 1989 Following the State Treaty of 15 May 1955, the Austrian National Council passed the Defence Act on 7 September

[1641] This created the legal prerequisites for the establishment and structuring of the new Austrian Armed Forces

[1642] After the occupying powers had lifted the ban on the formation of military facilities and the units of the B-Gendarmerie had been transformed into military units of the provisional border guard, initial considerations were made regarding the size, structure and tasks of the future Federal Army

[1643] The basis for these considerations and all other army formations up to 1972 were essentially defense considerations, which envisaged a defensive battle close to the border

[1644] On 11 January 1956, the Council of Ministers approved the 1956 Army Structure

[1645] It envisaged three groups of eight brigades and a further brigade in which army troops, air defense, schools, etc. would be brought together

[1646] This organization was designed for 60,000 soldiers, but in reality there were only 40,000 men

[1647] There were therefore considerations to establish a reserve army, for which there was initially no legal basis

[1648] At the end of the 1950s, it was therefore realized that it would not be possible to fill the given army framework and that the prerequisites for the existence of the army, an appropriate level of presence and a sufficient level of mobilization (assumed at that time to be 120,000 soldiers), could not be achieved

[1649] The relatively high number of mechanized vehicles and the experiences of the Hungarian crisis in 1956 led to greater importance being attached to armored units

[1650] On 1 August 1960, the 9th Armoured Brigade was established, and subsequently the 3rd Infantry was reorganised into the 3rd Armoured Brigade

[1651] These and other measures should lead to an increase in the operational readiness of the Federal Army units

[1655] The perspective for development was the Army structure of 1962, which came into effect in January 1963 and which, in order to ensure a constant, high level of operational readiness of as large a part of the peacetime army as possible, provided for a reorganization of the nine brigades into seven present brigades and three reserve brigades

[1656] These brigades included both operational units and training troops

[1657] The three group commands remained in place

[1658] Each group also had its own group troops

[1664] Due to the already low national defense budget at that time, it became clear that the personnel strengths required for this army structure could not be achieved

[1676] Based on the national defense doctrine of 1975 and the draft national defense plan of 1976, the concept of spatial defense was developed

[1677] “The state’s deterrence strategy finds its expression in the concept of spatial defense

[1678] This consists of an operational-tactical and a mental-psychological component, which together aim to integrate the army and the population

[1679] The concept of territorial defence envisaged coordinating the preparation and deployment of military forces in accordance with a territorial principle in direct cooperation between the civil and military sectors at all levels

[1680] A numerically strong militia army with a relatively short period of military service was intended to fulfil its defence mission through simplified combat operations, deployment in familiar areas, function-related selection and training of conscripts and the use of existing social ties

[1681] The defensive struggle should be started at the border and sustained against an aggressor along the lines of operations with the aim of wearing him down

[1682] The concept of area defense in Austria envisaged key zones in which the enemy’s penetration was to be prevented for a longer period of time, and area security zones to wear down enemy units that had already broken through

[1683] The strategic calculation behind this concept was to make a potential attacker marching through aware of the expectation of an operation with the highest possible entry and accommodation costs, in view of the loss of time and the attrition of his forces, and thus to achieve a deterrent effect

[1684] With the concept of spatial defense (embedded in the system of comprehensive national defense, the extensive implementation of the territorial principle, and the transition to a clear militia system in conjunction with a small standby force), a promising overall concept was found that was pursued by the Austrian Armed Forces throughout the entire final phase of the Cold War and also implemented to a large extent

[1772] Although this doctrine was not enacted in the form of a law, as a resolution of the National Council it represents a guiding basis for the Austrian Armed Forces in 2003/04 because it expresses the political will of this legislative body and thus of Austria

[1773] The doctrine is based on the principles of comprehensive security, preventive security (this principle emphasizes active participation in international conflict prevention and crisis management measures as a replacement for the threat response concept) and European solidarity (as a replacement for the concept of an autonomous security policy

[1774] The Security and Defence Doctrine contains the following recommendations, which have an impact on the development of the Austrian Armed Forces: a) Recommendations with a predominantly national reference

[1775] comprehensive information of the Austrian population about the security situation (with the participation of the Federal Armed Forces), - further development of the ULV into a system of comprehensive security precautions (with the participation of the Federal Armed Forces

[1776] Ensuring military defense capability, derived from the specific military-strategic situation through the ability to counter targeted attacks

[1777] Maintaining and further developing core military functions at a high technological level in an operationally effective force, •

[1778] Ensuring the growth capability of the armed forces, •

[1779] Ensuring constant airspace monitoring and security, •

[1780] Ensuring the defense against subconventional attacks and any conventional threats

[1781] b) Recommendations with a predominantly international focus

[1782] — European cooperation and intensification of intelligence information exchange, — further expansion of Austrian disaster relief in the international context, — making an appropriate contribution to international efforts for peacekeeping, conflict prevention, crisis management and post-crisis rehabilitation, —

[1783] Continuation of Austria’s engagement in international institutions (UN, OSCE, PfP, etc.), - Support for the further development of the ESDP and active and solidarity-based participation in the ESDP

[1793] The Military Strategic Concept is the holistic representation of the Federal Army with regard to its purpose and tasks, overall task capability, operational procedures, rough structure and scope of the subsystems and personnel structure and availability aspects for peace and deployment related to a medium- and long-term time horizon

[1794] It is derived from the strategic guidelines and is the binding basis for the other concepts derived from it at the military-strategic, operational, tactical and sub-area levels

[1795] International concepts are concepts of the EU, NATO or states that are considered as strategic partners for the Austrian Armed Forces, which are incorporated into the Austrian Armed Forces' conception due to their importance

[1799] Conceptual guidelines for the deployment of the Austrian Armed Forces. Military strategic positioning and objectives

[1800] The military strategic concept applicable in the period 2003/04 describes the deployment, tasks and capabilities of the Austrian Armed Forces on the basis of the still valid Army Structure 92/Structural Adjustment

[1801] This concept represents a clear shift from traditional military national defense to extended national defense in the sense of participation in international crisis management

[1802] The military-strategic framework shows that no existentially threatening aggression by conventional armed forces in the neighborhood is to be expected at present or in the foreseeable future

[1803] However, a potential, localized threat from air warfare means is not ruled out

[1804] Other threats in the subconventional and information warfare sectors are also addressed

[1805] Within the framework of territorial national defense, two central military-strategic objectives are addressed: containment (credible proof of Austria's ability to assert itself with military means against military dangers and threats) and security (preventing the spread of a crisis in the neighborhood without a direct threat or conveying a sense of security through the demonstrative presence of Federal Army forces in the endangered area

[1806] In the event of an armed conflict in the neighbourhood with direct repercussions for Austria, a corresponding, sustainable deterrent effect is to be achieved by concentrating appropriate forces of the Federal Army and by taking suitable defensive measures in the defence procedure

[1807] If this deterrent effect is not achieved, the defensive struggle should be started at the state border and, if possible, conducted in the area close to the border in order to seek a decision

[1808] The aim is to prevent an opponent from taking possession of its operational objectives in a sustainable manner, so that it cannot achieve any politically and strategically useful result

[1809] In the event of sub-conventional or subversive attacks on Austria, the undisturbed course of public life should be restored as quickly as possible

[1810] The military strategic objectives of holding and securing are still valid as fundamental objectives for operational deployment procedures within the framework of the respective military strategic situation, but due to the specific military strategic situation and the development of resources, they are increasingly losing their determining character for the size, organization and structure of the Federal Army

[1811] However, they continue to determine the qualitative capabilities of the armed forces

[1812] In addition to tasks in the area of national defence, military-strategic objectives in the context of international crisis management are becoming increasingly important

[1813] Support tasks within the framework of international peacekeeping, conflict prevention, conflict management and crisis rehabilitation

[1814] possible dangerous developments already in the strategic forefront and can therefore also be considered in a broader sense as part of military national defense

[1815] Thus, the ongoing security policy and military-strategic changes initiated a further development of the military-strategic conception towards the tasks of territorial protection, solidarity participation in peace support missions, and the maintenance and development of core military capabilities

[1816] The military strategic objective of solidarity in a multinational context as well as the structural requirements necessary to maintain basic tactical capabilities and to ensure territorial security precautions in a graduated form are therefore increasingly determining the strength of the Federal Army

[1817] Furthermore, in addition to the ability to provide national defence in the sense of managing a spatially limited defensive battle and participating in peace support operations, security police assistance operations (border area surveillance or property protection) as well as assistance operations to provide assistance in the event of natural disasters and accidents of exceptional magnitude are becoming essential objectives and tasks of the Federal Army

[1818] Operational and tactical basic assumptions

[1819] In general, in the event of a conventional war or other armed conflict in the neighborhood, the forces of the Federal Army deemed necessary are deployed in endangered or threatened areas in the form of a counterconcentration in order to demonstrate the ability to defend and thus achieve the objective of deterrence

[1820] In the case of disputes in the immediate vicinity without direct threat

[1821] within the framework of a security operation, the aim is to create the necessary deterrent effect through a security device and through demonstrative behavior

[1822] For this purpose, the forces of the Austrian Armed Forces will be trained according to basic operational

[1823] Deployment procedures used

[1824] However, the current military-strategic situation means that certain operational, cross-service deployment procedures, such as a security operation in the event of regional destabilisation in the immediate vicinity with varying effects on Austria, a defensive operation in the event of military conflicts in the neighbourhood with the risk of a direct spread to Austria or in the event of an attack directed directly against Austria in terms of concrete and comprehensive deployment preparations, are increasingly taking a back seat

[1825] In accordance with the military-strategic situation, however, elements of the area protection operational procedure are becoming more important in the case of subversive/subconventional threats

[1826] In line with the terrorist threat profile, the focus is on protecting strategic infrastructure (property protection), monitoring areas, maintaining special forces and reserves, and providing support and assistance to civil authorities and the population after attacks have occurred

[1827] In addition, based on the basic tactical and operational capabilities described above, there are those operational procedures that have emerged in the context of the development of the ESDP in a multinational scenario analysis, such as Separation of Parties by Force (SOP), Conflict Prevention (CP), Humanitarian Aid (HA), Evacuation Operations (EO) and Steady State (SS

[1828] Although the mastery of general tactical procedures (combined arms combat) is also the basis of these procedures, specific processes and content as well as interoperability are also the subject of general operational preparation and, in this sense, are of military strategic importance

[1829] The fulfilment of all the tasks described requires mastery of operational and tactical procedures

[1830] Mastering these procedures remains the fundamental and necessary basis for maintaining and developing the core military capabilities of the Austrian Armed Forces

[1831] In order to achieve the required effect, these procedures emphasize a high degree of combat mobility, with all the resulting organizational and technological consequences. Land forces are deployed in attack, defense, and delay modes

[1832] Added to this are hunting, fighting and protection

[1833] Types of use can also be used together

[1834] They are specified in more detail within the framework of tactics and combat technology and supplemented by other procedures such as reconnaissance, exploration, marching or surveillance

[1835] The basic types of use of air forces are air attack and air defense

[1836] They are supplemented by other procedures such as analysis, balance, perspective, for example, aerial reconnaissance, close air support, battlefield isolation or air transport

[1837] Airspace surveillance also serves, under normal circumstances, to prevent violations of Austrian airspace (preservation of air sovereignty

[1838] Prerequisites for deployment In order to carry out these tasks, the following essential prerequisites are mentioned: the operational readiness of commands, troops and agencies of the Federal Army in a graduated form, the assurance of personnel and logistical support, intelligence gathering and military security, information, public relations and the provision of resources for psychological support, the existence of an effective command and control system, territorial support, the ability to provide host nation support domestically, the inclusion of military interests in state crisis management and comprehensive national defense, the assurance of the necessary interoperability, well-established planning and command procedures and civil-military cooperation

[1839] Availability of the armed forces

[1840] An essential element for ensuring the availability and deployment of necessary armed forces is a graduated military-strategic response system

[1841] The aim is to respond appropriately to risks, hazards and threats using the necessary forces in combination with the system of flexible growth

[1842] These measures should also help to reduce, contain or eliminate risks to external and internal security

[1843] They range from consolidating intelligence gathering, increasing leadership capabilities, increasing logistical response capabilities, alerting measures and mobilization to the deployment of presence forces and mobilized forces

[1844] Based on the essential structural parameters of conscription, length of active service and militia system, the Austrian Armed Forces thus have a differentiated availability of forces, which in turn is decisive for the military-strategic response options

[1845] For this purpose, a flexible expansion of the armed forces is assumed (increasing the operational readiness of the Federal Army through a gradual increase in the provision of forces or a reaction with appropriate forces and measures in accordance with the respective situation

[1846] The flexible growth depends, among other things, on the availability of the basic military organization to the required extent, on the provision of rapidly available forces (especially presence forces) in the required strength and on the safeguarding of framework units as training, formation and mobilization bases

[1847] Therefore, the factor of constantly ready-to-use presence forces is of great importance

[1848] The term “rapidly available forces” refers to the 15,000 soldiers provided for in [Document Reference] 92/STRAN

[1849] The purpose of these forces is to ensure a military-strategic response capability to challenges of lower threat intensity as well as for assistance missions

[1850] These forces consist of 10,000 soldiers of the presence forces and 5,000 rapidly deployable soldiers of the militia

[1851] Structured presence forces are formed by specific associations, units and sub-units of the peacekeeping organization with the support of conscripts and are geared to specific operational tasks (presence tasks

[1852] These troops generally meet the requirements for a status as presence forces (operational readiness) for the first time during the fourth month of training of basic military service

[1853] A fixed call-up schedule ensures consistent year-round availability of these on-site forces

[1854] Furthermore, the need for presence forces for international operations, consisting exclusively of volunteer professional and long-serving soldiers or commissioned militia soldiers, is also addressed

[1855] The deployment of structured presence forces can be based on the following criteria

[1856] White Paper 2004 Analysis Balance Perspectives ¾ from the end of the third month of training for guard and security duties (under normal peacetime conditions), ¾ from the completion of basic training (usually after the fourth month of training) for qualified assistance in the event of natural disasters and accidents of exceptional magnitude or within the framework of a security operation (low risk intensity) or a security police assistance operation

[1857] Fulfillment of all tasks stipulated by military law (provided that the troops are ready for deployment based on training) from the end of the sixth month of training

[1954] The United Nations Standby Arrangements System (UNSAS), implemented since April 1994, is comparable to a database in which troopcontributing nations register the elements they intend to deploy for peacekeeping operations or disaster relief missions

[1957] United Nations Standby High Readiness Brigade

[1959] The headquarters of the international brigade command is located in Denmark

[2038] The current situation of the Federal Army

[2039] The Austrian Armed Forces, as the armed force of the Republic of Austria, bear the name Austrian Federal Army (ÖBH) and are essentially divided into the Land Forces (LaSK) and the Air Force (LuSK

[2040] Like the Central Office, the Austrian Armed Forces (ÖBH) is part of the Federal Ministry of Defence and has a peacetime and operational organisation, which are characterised by the principles of general conscription and the militia system

[2041] The organizational structure of the Austrian Armed Forces (ÖBH) (Army Structure/HG) is based on political and strategic guidelines and is primarily oriented towards threats, the defense system and the available resources

[2042] Multinational guidelines and cooperation are becoming increasingly important

[2043] The forces or troops of the Federal Army are deployed with varying levels of availability depending on the occasion or purpose

[2044] The spectrum basically ranges from forces available at short notice for assistance missions to the deployment of mobilized forces within the scope of the entire operational organization for the purposes of military national defense

[2045] In addition to the land and air forces, the Austrian Armed Forces (ÖBH) has other organizational units, such as the Special Operations Command, the International Operations Command, the Command for Command Support, the Operational Support Command, and the offices and departments subordinate to the Central Office

[2046] The LaSK and LuSK are essentially the instruments that fulfil the tasks of the Austrian Armed Forces through established procedures

[2047] For this purpose, they have specific equipment and weapon systems at their disposal within the framework of the assigned troops

[2048] In addition to the legally standardized tasks, the security and defense doctrine, the military strategic concept from 2001 and its revisions in the following years represent the essential guidelines for the Federal Army

[2049] In addition, there are international obligations and cooperation within the framework of the EU, NATO/PfP, UN and OSCE

[2050] The current organizational structure of the Austrian Armed Forces results, on the one hand, from the Army Structure 92 in the form of the Structural Adjustment 98 and, on the other hand, from the reorganization of the top/upper leadership in

[2051] In total, the Federal Ministry of Defence (including the conscripts who are permanently available on an annual average) consists of approximately 45,000 people

[2053] Force personnel achieve and maintain an appropriate level of training as part of their service

[2054] Militia forces generally maintain and expand their acquired level of training through regular, recurring exercises

[2055] In light of the increasing importance of the multinational commitment of the Austrian Armed Forces (ÖBH), the VOREIN (Prepared Units) principle was introduced several years ago to ensure the preparation of certain organizational elements of the ÖBH for international missions

[2056] Currently, the VOREIN principle within the framework of the Forces for International Operations (KIOP) is increasingly being supplemented or replaced by the principle of cadre presence units (KPE

[2057] KPE are units that are made up exclusively of professional soldiers and temporary soldiers and are permanently available

[2060] It is planned to reduce the duration of basic military service from eight to six months starting in 2006, which is expected to result in changes in the deployment of basic military service personnel, particularly in connection with security police assistance missions

[2061] In principle, the personnel groups represented in the Federal Ministry of Defence and the Federal Army are soldiers (officers, non-commissioned officers, recruits) and civilian employees

[2062] Since 1998, women have been able to serve as soldiers on a voluntary basis, with no restrictions on function or training

[2064] Since the security policy shift at the beginning of the 1990s, the Austrian Armed Forces (ÖBH) has been undergoing a multi-stage restructuring and reform process that is still ongoing. This process was initiated with the Army Structure 92 and is currently taking its current form with the ÖBH 2010 reform

[2065] In principle, this involves the transformation of the Austrian armed forces from the army of a small neutral state, which was primarily oriented towards national defense and had to ward off potential aggressors after mobilization, to a multinationally oriented army with a high proportion of present cadre forces, which, in addition to maintaining Austria's sovereignty and protecting the population, makes Austria's military contribution within the framework of international solidarity

[2066] Functional areas of responsibility of the armed forces. Functional areas of responsibility represent the Austrian Armed Forces according to main tasks and essential characteristics

[2071] Troops and branches of arms

[2072] The branches of the military are composed of different branches of service depending on their functional purpose. Many operational tasks can only be fulfilled by the units of the Federal Army through the cooperation of the various branches of service

[2073] Combined arms combat is also the fundamental capability for fulfilling the tasks of the Federal Army in peace, in crisis, and in the face of a military threat

[2075] This results from the high demand for infantry forces for such tasks

[2076] The term branch of service is a designation for the classification of a troop according to the nature of its use or its main equipment

[2077] The branches of the military include: NBC defense troops, artillery troops, reconnaissance troops, signals troops, anti-aircraft troops, aviation troops, fighter troops, fighter commando troops, air surveillance troops, material maintenance troops, supply troops, public order troops, armored infantry troops, tank destroyer troops, armored troops, engineer troops, medical troops, staff troops, transport troops, guard troops, and economic troops. In contrast, the term "branch of service" refers to the branches of the military grouped together according to their functional purpose

[2080] The command troops include: staff troops, reconnaissance troops, airspace surveillance troops, signals troops and public order troops

[2084] Combat support troops can also carry out independent combat tasks

[2085] The combat support troops include artillery troops, engineer troops, NBC defense troops and elements of the air force

[2086] The logistics troops are the branch of the military whose main task is the implementation of logistical measures within the framework of operational support

[2089] Planning in the Federal Army Long-term planning is of essential importance for all those organizations that are expected to fulfill tasks in the best possible way, on the one hand with the “uncertainty factor” of future environmental developments and, on the other hand, with relatively limited flexibility regarding the use of resources

[2090] It has a "co-creative" or preparatory function in the development of relevant political guidelines, and on the other hand, a "prescriptive" role for further military planning. As a result of this formative military participation, a current "situation report" is provided to policymakers within the framework of a (pro-)active dialogue, taking primarily military aspects into account. This report includes recommendations and various options (force models

[2091] This military contribution, prepared for a political decision, is intended to result in a consensual (or, if possible, broadly accepted) political directive to ensure a targeted and resourceconsistent armed forces development

[2092] Prescribing role" means the provision of a "policy document" (military strategic concept) and a derived, more specific core document (planning guideline), which together form a secure basis for further military planning

[2093] In doing so, fundamental objectives, task scenarios, and the necessary military capabilities are defined, taking into account legal foundations and political requirements. Planning areas and planning cycle: The subject of Austrian Armed Forces planning is the organization of the army, its armament, garrisoning, and designation of troops

[2094] This includes conception, structuring, budgeting and implementation and relates to the three expenditure areas of personnel, operations and investments

[2095] The Federal Army planning is divided into concept, structure, program, implementation and financial planning

[2096] Conceptual planning is part of the Federal Army’s strategic planning

[2097] It plays a formative role in the development of political principles and guidelines (e.g. security doctrine or partial strategy of defence policy

[2098] The conceptual planning also specifies the medium- to long-term development of the Federal Army (objectives, tasks

[2099] The specifications for conceptual planning arise from political objectives, legal bases, the expected threat profile and any international obligations

[2100] The conceptual planning describes the aggregate states of the operational forces (modular, tailor-made composition) in the various cases of military task fulfillment in accordance with Article 79 of the Federal Constitutional Law

[2101] It also specifies the measures to achieve these objectives and the priorities in line with the resource situation

[2102] Structural planning regulates, initiates and controls the concrete structural development of the Federal Army organization

[2103] This refers to the participation in the development of conceptual documents and the planning implementation of these documents and specifications for the structure of the ÖBH

[2104] This is done by defining concrete tasks and a derived determination of the structures with regard to organization, personnel (including their training), materials and infrastructure

[2105] The structure plan thus provides the target values, which are then compared with the actual values

[2106] The necessary requirements to meet future demand will be reflected in the investment plan to be drawn up

[2107] Overall, program planning, in close coordination with financial planning, ensures the entire short- and medium-term planning and control of the use of all resources of the Austrian Armed Forces (personnel, operations, investments

[2108] Program planning refers to the creation of concrete, immediately implementable programs and is coordinated with the budget preparation process

[2109] The results of the program planning are initially presented in draft sub-programs (training, organizational, regulatory, personnel, operational, armament, construction and research programs) and, after a coordination process, are summarized in the implementation program

[2110] The implementation program, in conjunction with the financial plan, forms the basis for the preparation of the annual budget (federal estimate) and is adopted annually

[2111] The implementation program, together with the financial plan, forms the basis for relevant reports within the framework of international planning processes (EU, NATO/PfP, UN and OSCE

[2112] Implementation planning refers to the concrete planning of the provision of personnel, materials, infrastructure, etc., as well as the "implementation" of the necessary changes in tasks and structures based on the specifications of the program planning

[2113] Deployment planning is the planning of the coordinated provision of personnel, materials and the provision of ready-to-use infrastructure

[2114] In addition to concrete procurement planning for armaments, including introduction planning, the main objective is ultimately to bring together trained personnel with the appropriate material to form functional organizational elements

[2115] An essential basis for all planning areas is financial planning, which takes into account the actual financial requirements

[2116] Financial planning is an integral part of planning in all areas

[2117] It includes the systematic planning and management of financial resources in the form of a comparison of expenditures and revenues (taking into account all requirements of the Federal Army), starting with a long-term budget forecast and ending with short-term financial planning as a basis for the immediate budget preparation

[2118] The most important task of financial planning is to align the plans with the financial resource situation by mapping the respective planning results in the financial plan

[2119] Another key task is monitoring the development of the financial structure, primarily in the areas of personnel, operations and investments

[2120] The Austrian Armed Forces' planning takes the form of a two-year cyclical planning and review process, which is coordinated with national and international requirements

[2121] The purpose of this planning is to develop and review planning objectives derived from the core document (planning guidelines), taking into account the resources available for this purpose, which increases the conformity of the Federal Army's planning to the objectives and, on the other hand, optimizes the degree of objective achievement

[2122] This planning process is therefore an instrument for periodic goal review

[2123] Leadership Political and military leadership

[2124] The strategic leadership of the Republic of Austria is exercised by the political leadership bodies of the state leadership (the Federal President, the National Council, the Federal Government, the Federal Minister of Defence and, in special cases, the State Governor(s

[2125] At this level, for example, security policy objectives are formulated

[2126] From this perspective, the Federal Ministry of Defence, as an auxiliary body of the Federal Minister, is also part of the strategic leadership

[2127] In particular, it carries out the tasks of military strategy in its area and defines goals in the areas of the defense system, army structure, military strategic procedure and mobilization system

[2128] The Federal Minister of Defence exercises the command authority delegated to him over the Austrian Armed Forces through the commanders

[2129] The military leadership is subordinate to the political or strategic leadership (“The Primacy of Politics”) and has the task of implementing the tasks/orders set by the political leadership within the framework established by the legislature

[2130] It is permeated by the principles of “command and obedience,” “undivided personal responsibility of the military leader,” and “consistency of mission and means.”

[2131] In principle, military leadership tasks within the departmental area of the Federal Ministry of Defence are carried out at the military strategic, operational and tactical leadership levels

[2132] The military strategic leadership is the responsibility of the Federal Ministry of Defence and is organizationally represented in the central office

[2133] Operational command is essentially the responsibility of the Ground Forces Command, the Air Force Command, the International Operations Command and the Special Operations Command

[2134] Tactical leadership is essentially the responsibility of the commands of large and small units (brigades, regiments, battalions) and, in some areas, also of the military commands

[2135] The military and civilian leaders – primarily the commanders – have, within the scope of their function, legally recognized authority, which includes the command authority and responsibility towards the forces and resources under their command with regard to their targeted deployment to fulfill a mission

[2136] To fulfil his command duties, the commander (from small units upwards) has a staff at his disposal, which brings together the necessary command and support personnel

[2137] In general, each staff consists of a Chief of Staff (or Head of Staff Work) and the General Staff or Staff Departments or the Specialist Departments

[2181] Management structure for national and international tasks

[2186] Management positions and their tasks

[2187] The Central Office of the Federal Ministry of Defence The Cabinet of the Federal Minister (KBM) is responsible for matters relating to the adjutant service for the Federal Minister, matters relating to the advice and support of the Federal Minister in his decisions, matters relating to the intra- and interministerial coordination of security and defence policy and matters relating to social issues brought directly to the attention of the Federal Minister

[2188] General Council – The restructuring of the Central Office within the framework of REORG 2002 also made it necessary to create a successor organization to the management staff of the Federal Ministry of Defence

[2189] The General Council is responsible for assessing the security policy and military-strategic situation on an ad hoc basis and, based on this, proposing strategic decisions regarding deployment options for the Federal Army to the Federal Minister of Defence

[2190] The General Council meets after being convened by the Chief of the General Staff under his chairmanship and consists in principle of the heads of departments, the Chief of Cabinet, the heads of staff in the Federal Ministry of Defence, the Head of the Directorate for Security Policy, the Head of the Legal and Legislative Service Group, the Heads of the Army Intelligence Office and the Defense Office, and the Head of the General Staff Office

[2191] The Directorate for Security Policy (DirSichPol) encompasses security policy matters, security policy research matters, and matters relating to the Office for Security Policy

[2192] These powers also include advising the Federal Minister or the Federal Ministry of Defence and Consumer Protection in matters of security policy

[2193] In addition, the head of the directorate is also an advisory member of the National Security Council

[2194] The Central Section encompasses presidential and budgetary matters, legal and legislative service matters, personnel and supplementary staff matters, and departmental communications matters, including the areas of press, communications strategy, and marketing

[2195] The Control Section (KontrS) encompasses matters relating to reports and the White Paper, matters relating to disciplinary and complaints procedures, matters relating to process and outcome control, as well as matters relating to internal auditing and financial control

[2196] Furthermore, the Control Section forms the interface between the Federal Ministry of Defence and the Office of the Federal Armed Forces Complaints Commission

[2197] The General Staff (GStb) essentially consists of the General Staff Directorate, the Command Staff, the Planning Staff and the Armaments Staff

[2201] He supports the Federal Minister of Defence in the exercise of the right of disposal and the authority to give commands in accordance with Article 2 and 3 of the Federal Constitutional Law

[2202] The Chief of the General Staff is an advisory member of the National Security Council, chairman of the Working Committee "M" within the ULV, advisor to the Austrian Armed Forces Complaints Commission, and representative of the Austrian Armed Forces in the EU Military Committee (EUMC), the Coordination Committee of the Euro-Atlantic Partnership, and relevant multinational bodies

[2205] The Head of the General Staff Directorate is Deputy Chief of the General Staff

[2209] The command staff is generally capable of carrying out its tasks over a longer period of time, with the use of reinforcements, on the basis of 24-hour staff work, 7 days a week

[2210] The Armaments Staff (RüstStb) encompasses matters of armaments policy, armaments, information and communications technology, construction, central technical, and materials management

[2211] The Planning Staff (PlStb) is responsible for the matters of conceptual planning (military strategy, overall military planning, business administration and financial management), structural and program planning and organization of the Federal Army

[2294] The reorganization had the following objectives: ¾ Adaptation of the department's command structure to the reduced troop size in accordance with the structural adjustment to Army Structure 92, ¾ Alignment of the command structure to requirements arising from the Federal Army's participation in multinational security structures, ¾ Concentration of strategic matters in the central office and delegation of operational tasks to the subordinate area, ¾

[2295] Reallocation of personnel resources to the troops by streamlining structures and delegating tasks, ¾ Concentration of military competencies for planning and provision of the Austrian Armed Forces (ÖBH) as well as for supporting the Federal Minister in exercising the right of disposal and command over the ÖBH under a newly created Chief of the General Staff, ¾ Organization of branches of the armed forces (land and air forces

[2318] Within the framework of the Federal Ministry of Defence and its subordinate agencies and commands, the structures and measures of internal control are of fundamental importance

[2319] In addition to the basic task of supervisory authority (at all management levels), internal control mechanisms are responsible for the tasks of inspection (at the KdoLaSK level), process and result control, as well as internal auditing and financial control (at the BMLV level

[2320] In addition, there is the area of disciplinary and grievance matters

[2322] Control and audit

[2323] Process and result control

[2324] In the Control Section, the Process and Result Control Group (GrpKontr) carries out the tasks assigned in accordance with the business allocation as accompanying control (process control) and as subsequent control (result control) in all planning and implementation phases of armed forces planning/development and armed forces command

[2325] The GrpKontr is also responsible for reviewing personnel and material security measures within the framework of the military security service, unless this is performed by the legal protection officer in accordance with the Military Powers Act

[2326] Furthermore, GrpKontr is responsible for monitoring the safety and protection of all department members in accordance with the relevant standards

[2327] White Paper 2004 Analysis Balance Sheet Perspectives Analysis Balance Sheet

[2328] In particular, it supports the Federal Minister as head of the authority in carrying out his duties under the Federal Civil Servants Protection Act

[2329] The organizational scope of GrpKontr extends to the central office and to the subordinate offices and institutions in Germany and abroad

[2330] The task of GrpKontr is to monitor the fulfillment of tasks in all planning and implementation phases in the process of armed forces planning/development and armed forces command, as well as the development of optimization and rationalization proposals, including the associated control system

[2331] This task includes, in particular, the monitoring of requirements planning and management measures, the monitoring of the achievement of the capability profiles of military organizational elements, and participation in the summary treatment of the Court of Auditors' inspection, activity and other reports

[2332] The accompanying control (process control) identifies any potential problems and undesirable developments that are due to non-compliance with laws, administrative standards and issued guidelines, instructions, concepts, etc., as they arise, so that decision-makers can take measures to remedy them at an early stage

[2333] This does not affect the undivided responsibility of the decision-makers responsible according to the business allocation

[2334] The purpose and objective of subsequent control (result control) is to determine whether organizational elements have achieved their objectives in relation to the specifications and available resources

[2335] Where appropriate, sources of error are identified and suggestions for solutions are developed to enable their elimination within the framework of planning and management measures

[2336] The subsequent control is carried out

[2337] as a system control, generally in the form of commission or individual audits

[2338] Internal audit and financial control

[2339] The Internal Audit and Financial Control Group (GrpRev) supports the Federal Minister in his management function by monitoring the effectiveness and efficiency of the specialist and audit areas defined in accordance with the business allocation and reports on the audit results

[2340] In addition, it advises the specialist departments and contributes to the achievement of departmental objectives through internal auditing

[2341] It monitors compliance with the principles of financial management and the safeguarding of assets by specifically observing whether the principles of orderliness and expediency, as well as efficiency and economy, are observed in the administrative processes

[2342] The Audit Group carries out the assigned tasks as accompanying controls (prevision) and as subsequent audits (audits) in the form of individual case audits or system audits

[2343] The focus is on the accompanying control of major projects and the monitoring of contract awards

[2344] The organizational scope of the GrpRev extends to the central office and to the subordinate offices and institutions in Germany and abroad

[2345] The audit is generally carried out in the form of a result- and process-oriented audit

[2346] The result-oriented audit deals with the results of the tasks of the respective specialist and audit department with regard to target conformity, while the process-oriented audit deals with the appropriateness and cost-effectiveness of the process itself

[2347] The accompanying control (prevention) is intended to avoid any inappropriateness in the performance of administrative tasks

[2348] Furthermore, it identifies undesirable and harmful developments that are due to non-compliance with laws, administrative norms and principles of management as they arise

[2349] Prevention is carried out by monitoring the fulfilment of tasks in all planning and implementation phases and by developing proposals for optimisation and rationalisation in the process of armed forces planning and development, including the associated control system, in particular by monitoring compliance with award and procurement standards, reviewing the awarding of major contracts, providing advice on the planning and implementation of major projects, as well as in the preparation of procurement programmes and financing plans and in the adoption of important organisational measures and procedural regulations

[2350] The purpose of subsequent auditing (auditing) is to retrospectively assess compliance with laws, administrative standards, regulatory compliance and the fulfillment of specified objectives in the course of a critical examination of defined organizational structures and of previously completed management activities

[2351] The revision can

[2352] White Paper 2004 Analysis Balance Sheet Perspectives as a system audit or as a regularity audit

[2353] The audit is carried out by monitoring compliance with legality, management principles, efficiency, economy and expediency, in particular by examining organizational structures and the deployment of personnel, examining the effects of service instructions, monitoring cash and accounting systems, developing rationalization proposals and suggestions for improving organizational and procedural structures, summarizing the Court of Auditors' inspection, activity and other reports, and advising on the conclusions from the Court of Auditors' reports at the request of the organizational units responsible for this according to the division of business

[2358] The observance of official duties by employees and the expediency, efficiency and economy of the administration of office
