[2369] Disciplinary and Complaints Matters: Disciplinary Law

[2370] Soldiers are subject to their own disciplinary law, which is regulated in the Army Disciplinary Act (HDG

[2371] Conscripts in the militia and reserve ranks who hold at least the rank of corporal and retired public servants are also subject to this disciplinary law

[2372] Every soldier bears responsibility for his comrades and the equipment entrusted to him

[2373] The Austrian Armed Forces can only fulfill its mission if every soldier accepts his or her responsibilities and takes the associated duties seriously

[2374] If a soldier culpably neglects his duties, he can be held accountable

[2375] Punishment is intended to deter the offender and his comrades from further breaches of duty in order not to endanger the reputation of the office or essential interests of the service, in particular order and discipline

[2376] The disciplinary procedure is a legal procedure involving two instances, which concludes with a decision in the event of conviction

[2377] There is the possibility of appealing against final disciplinary decisions to the Constitutional Court or the Administrative Court

[2378] According to the Hdg 2002, there is the commander procedure, which is to be applied to all soldiers, and the commission procedure, which is to be applied to soldiers in service if a higher penalty than the fine is to be imposed

[2379] In the commander procedure, a commander, from the unit commander upwards, is the disciplinary authority

[2380] The focus here is on the speed and immediacy required by military operations and operational requirements, based on a strict legal procedure

[2381] In the commission procedure, a senate of three members decides on breaches of duty by soldiers in their employment

[2382] The Senate President carries out his duties full-time

[2383] One of the assessors is appointed by the Central Committee

[2384] In the second instance, the Higher Disciplinary Commission for Soldiers decides, which is also divided into senates of three people

[2385] The Senate members are not subject to instructions in their function

[2386] The employer’s representative is the disciplinary lawyer, who is also a party to the proceedings

[2387] Penalties ranging from a reprimand to 350% of the monthly salary can be imposed, and in particularly serious cases even dismissal or demotion, which for employees entails the loss of all rights arising from their employment

[2388] In use according to § 2 para. 1 lit

[2389] a and b WG 2001 and on foreign missions, soldiers are subject to the deployment regulations of the HDG

[2390] There is only the commander procedure

[2391] To decide on the penalties imposed only during operations, namely disciplinary detention, disciplinary arrest and demotion, an operational disciplinary body, which is independent of instructions, is provided for in the second instance

[2392] After the end of the assignment, a review by the disciplinary authority responsible for the assignment is possible

[2393] The disciplinary procedure under the Army Disciplinary Act is efficient, quick and easy to apply, while the accused's rights as a party are preserved and review at the appeal level and appeal to the public law courts are possible

[2394] Disciplinary law is an important tool for the commander to punish breaches of duty and maintain order and discipline

[2395] But problems cannot be solved with punishment alone

[2396] The commander must also consider other leadership measures to be taken in addition to or instead of punishment

[2397] More and more soldiers on foreign missions will be entrusted with tasks that require tight leadership

[2398] Disciplinary proceedings will then become increasingly important as a management tool

[2399] The procedure should be carried out quickly, while respecting the rights of the parties and the principles of the rule of law

[2400] Civilian civil servants are subject to disciplinary law under the Civil Service Act (BDG

[2401] It is also a commission procedure in which a senate consisting of the chairperson and two other members decides

[2402] Penalties range from reprimands and fines to five months' salary or even dismissal

[2403] Complaints system Every soldier has the right to complain about deficiencies and grievances in the military service that affect him, in particular about injustice suffered or interference with his official powers (ordinary complaint

[2404] The unit commander is responsible for dealing with the ordinary complaint

[2405] In the ordinary complaints procedure, immediacy is paramount, with the outcome intended to remedy grievances within the military organisation in the long term and ensure industrial peace

[2406] Every conscript, every soldier and every member of the militia and reserve ranks may complain about deficiencies and grievances affecting him directly to the Federal Army Complaints Commission (extraordinary complaint

[2407] The Federal Armed Forces Complaints Commission examines the complaints and makes a recommendation to the Federal Minister

[2408] The extraordinary complaint shall be dealt with by the Federal Minister taking into account the recommendation of the Federal Armed Forces Complaints Commission

[2409] Any complaint from outsiders who feel they have been adversely affected by the Federal Army in any way will also be investigated

[2410] Furthermore, so-called “disciplinary complaints” regarding deficiencies in service operations are dealt with

[2411] The Federal Armed Forces Complaints Commission is a collegial body consisting of three chairmen and six other members

[2412] The chairpersons are appointed by the National Council on the basis of a joint proposal from the Main Committee; the remaining members are nominated by the political parties in proportion to their number of seats in the Main Committee of the National Council

[2413] The term of office of the Federal Armed Forces Complaints Commission is six years, with the chairpersons alternating in office every two years

[2414] The Chief of the General Staff and another departmental official to be appointed by the Federal Minister serve as advisory members of the Federal Armed Forces Complaints Commission

[2415] In addition to examining complaints, the Federal Army Complaints Commission can also investigate suspected deficiencies and abuses in the military sector on its own initiative

[2416] The chairmen of the Federal Army Complaints Commission for the period from 1 January 2003 to 31 December 2008 are the MPs

[2417] Former MP Paul Kiss, the MP

[2418] NR Anton Gaal and Editor-in-Chief Brig Prof. Walter Seledec

[2419] Every two years, the Federal Minister of Defence submits the annual reports of the Federal Armed Forces Complaints Commission to the National Council, including a statement on the recommendations

[2420] The Federal Ministry of Defence and Consumer Protection provides the Federal Armed Forces Complaints Commission with the necessary personnel and material resources

[2421] Although the staff provided are part of the staff of the Federal Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Consumer Protection, they are bound by the instructions of the acting chairman in matters relating to the Complaints Commission, in accordance with the Constitution

[2422] The Federal Minister has appointed a Legal Protection Commissioner in accordance with the Military Powers Act

[2423] Its task is to review the legality of the actions of the military intelligence services (AbwA and HNaA) – particularly with regard to suspected violations of fundamental rights or unlawful use of data

[2424] The term of office of the Legal Protection Commissioner is three years

[2425] Since 1 July 2001, the function of Legal Protection Commissioner has been held by Graz criminal law professor DDr

[2426] Karlheinz Probst

[2427] His deputies are the former OGH President Hon.-Prof

[2428] Dr. Herbert Steininger and the former head of section in the BMLV, Dr. Franz Sailler

[2429] The Legal Protection Commissioner prepares an annual report on his or her audit activities, which is submitted to the Federal Minister of Defence for submission to the National Council’s Standing Subcommittee for the Examination of Intelligence Measures to Ensure Military National Defence

[2430] Any deficiencies identified therein will be remedied by the Federal Minister of Defence

[2431] In the event of accidents involving personal injury or property damage and other incidents involving military vehicles, weapons and ammunition, an investigation commission consisting of a leader, a legally qualified member and other expert members will be appointed

[2432] The task of the commission of inquiry is to determine the cause and, if necessary, to develop proposals to prevent similar cases from occurring

[2433] Based on the investigation reports, the Federal Ministry of Defence will take measures to remedy and prevent future violations and, if necessary, initiate disciplinary or criminal proceedings

[2434] In the area of disciplinary and complaints management, investigations into complaints submitted to the Ombudsman's Office are carried out and measures are taken to remedy identified grievances, provided that a well-founded determination of the facts is necessary to prepare a response to the Ombudsman's Office

[2594] Austria's positive development for future challenges depends largely on a future-oriented science and research policy

[2595] Therefore, the government has always emphasized the objective of doing everything possible to ensure that Austria remains competitive in the field of research and technology

[2596] The general considerations of the Security and Defence Doctrine also state that a modern and future-oriented security policy is based on preventing the emergence of risks and threats through preventive measures

[2597] This gives new weight to the instruments of security policy action, whereby, in addition to political, military, police, intelligence and economic instruments, educational, information and communication policy and social instruments are also used

[2598] For these reasons, the science and research department at the Federal Ministry of Defence is an essential element of overall military planning

[2599] Military Research

[2600] Military research is systematic scientific activity aimed at gaining new knowledge for military national defense

[2601] Their implementation can be the responsibility of both internal and external departments and institutions

[2602] According to the system of scientific disciplines, military science research is divided into the areas of humanities and social science research, natural science and military technology research, and military medicine research

[2603] The types of research are differentiated according to basic research, applied research and experimental research

[2604] Basic research comprises original investigations with the purpose of increasing the state of knowledge without being directed towards a specific practical goal

[2605] Applied research also involves original investigations with the purpose of increasing knowledge, but directed towards a specific goal

[2606] Experimental development is the systematic application of knowledge with the aim of producing new and significantly improved materials, devices, products, processes or systems

[2607] Basic research is therefore rather an exception, because pure research activity is not one of the direct tasks of the BMLV

[2608] Applied research accounts for the largest part of military science research

[2609] Experimental development applies particularly to the areas of scientific/defense technology and military medical research

[2610] Organization and structure

[2611] A research advisory board was established at the Federal Ministry of Defence to coordinate research matters

[2612] The Research Advisory Board includes the Chief of the General Staff as chairman, the Head of the Planning Staff as acting chairman and the representatives of the Cabinet of the Federal Minister, the Directorate for Security Policy, the Central and Control Section, the Planning Staff, the Armaments Staff, the Command Staff, the Department of Overall Military Planning, the National Defence Academy, the Theresian Military Academy, the Army Intelligence Office, the Defence Office and the Chairman of the Scientific Commission as permanent members

[2613] The Department of Military Planning acts as the secretariat of the Research Advisory Board

[2614] The Research Advisory Board is responsible, among other things, for preparing all documents required for the Chief of the General Staff to advise the Federal Minister on research matters

[2615] Furthermore, the Research Advisory Board draws up a military science research program for the department (catalogue of research topics

[2616] In addition, the Research Advisory Board coordinates all military science research projects in the Austrian Armed Forces, sets priorities accordingly, ensures the funding of research projects and issues requirements within the framework of military security

[2617] Responsibility for the coordination of all scientific matters and matters relating to military science research lies with the Military Overall Planning Department (MGP) in the Planning Staff of the Federal Ministry of Defence and Defense

[2618] Among other things, she is responsible for coordinating research and affairs of the Scientific Commission and the Research Advisory Board

[2619] This office is therefore the central coordination office for research in the Federal Army

[2620] At the same time, it acts as the secretariat of the Research Advisory Board, as the secretariat of the Scientific Commission and as the liaison office for cooperation with the Austrian Academy of Sciences (ÖAW

[2621] In this function, the department has the authority to issue orders for research to be carried out at the academies, offices, schools and other subordinate departments

[2622] The MGP also acts as the interface to national and international research-related institutions and organizations and represents the Federal Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry, Environment and Water Management in all research matters

[2623] After initial considerations had already been made in 1986 as to how the departmental intentions could be better linked with the resources of the Austrian universities, the Humanities and Social Sciences Commission at the Federal Ministry of Defence (GSK) was established under Federal Minister Dr. Lichal with effect from 1 January

[2624] With effect from 1 July 1992, Federal Minister Dr. Fasslabend established the Science Commission at the BMLV as the successor organization to the GSK

[2625] This commission consists of members appointed by the Federal Minister on the proposal of the research bodies of the BMLV and is divided into the Executive Committee and the Scientific Advisory Boards

[2626] The Commission currently consists of 34 members, including 96 external and 38 internal members

[2627] In addition to a wide range of scientists and departmental staff, the commission also includes representatives from other federal ministries, federal agencies and non-university research institutions such as the Seibersdorf Research Center and Joanneum Research

[2628] The Scientific Commission carries out its work primarily in the scientific advisory boards

[2629] In addition to the Advisory Board for Strategic and Social Sciences, the Science Commission has an Advisory Board for Military History, a Military Technology and Natural Sciences, a Military Medicine and an Economics Advisory Board

[2630] The main tasks of the Science Commission are to advise the Federal Minister on issues of science and research directly and indirectly relevant to the department, to support the planning and teaching needs of the department, to utilize scientific expertise for the needs of the department and to establish, maintain and deepen contacts with scientific institutions

[2631] By resolution of the general meeting of the Austrian Academy of Sciences on 4 March 1994, the Commission of the Austrian Academy of Sciences for Scientific Cooperation with Departments of the Federal Ministry of Defence was founded

[2632] After the Science Commission at the Federal Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Consumer Protection was established in 1992, it subsequently became necessary to organize an institutionalized cooperation with the country's highest authority in the field of science and research, the Austrian Academy of Sciences

[2633] This academy can be described on the one hand as a “scholarly society” and on the other hand as the largest provider of non-university basic research in Austria

[2634] The objective of the commission is to obtain financial support from the Austrian Ministry for basic research projects by members of the Austrian Academy of Sciences whose questions also have a certain relevance

[2635] On the other hand, the Federal Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry, Environment and Water Management (BMLV) is taking advantage of the opportunity to allocate research needs not met in its own area to members of Austria's highest-ranking scientific institution

[2636] The Commission serves to facilitate cooperation between departments of the Federal Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry, Environment and Water Management and the Austrian Academy of Sciences in all scientific fields of mutual interest and uses all means deemed appropriate within the framework of applicable laws and regulations

[2637] The main tasks of the Commission are the coordination of cooperation between departments of the Federal Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Consumer Protection and the Austrian Academy of Sciences, the approval of scientific projects before they are submitted to the Research Advisory Board, the establishment of contacts and the dissemination of information in the mutual interest of the Federal Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Consumer Protection and the Austrian Academy of Sciences

[2638] The scientific disciplines of this commission cover the fields of strategy and security policy, strategic situation, geoinformation, historical sciences and museology, geosciences and material strength, physics and space research, cryptology, and psychology and medicine

[2639] The main tasks of the Directorate for Security Policy, which is organized within the Federal Ministry of Defence and directly subordinate to the Federal Minister, are to advise the Federal Minister and the departments of the ministry on security policy issues and to organize and manage scientific research in the field of international security policy

[2640] To this end, the Directorate strives for close ties with the National Defence Academy (Institute for Strategy and Security Policy/ISS, Institute for Peacekeeping and Conflict Management/IFK, Institute for Military Sociology and Military Education/IMM) and cooperation with renowned domestic and foreign research institutes and personalities

[2641] The Office for Security Policy is assigned to the Directorate for Security Policy in the Federal Ministry of Defence and Consumer Protection as a directly subordinate department of the Federal Ministry of Defence and Consumer Protection

[2642] This office is divided into a security policy department, research management, a leadership and information technology department, a publications department, and administration

[2643] In particular, the National Defence Academy, as a research institution subordinate to the Federal Ministry of Defence and Consumer Protection with numerous scientific experts, covers primarily scientific disciplines related to national security

[2644] These include, for example, strategic fundamentals, international security, armed forces and society, military education and military linguistics

[2645] The Army History Museum (military history research), the Office for Armaments and Defense Technology (technical and scientific research) and the Army Hospital (military medical research) are also subordinate research institutions

[2662] Structure and Organization of the Federal Army

[2663] The basis for the military-strategic implementation of the 2001 Security and Defence Doctrine is the structural adjustment of the Army structure in 1992 (HG 92/STRAN), which was adopted from 1 April 1998, taking into account the security policy developments and the resource situation at the time, and which also applied in 2003/04 (with the exception of the reorganisation of the top/senior leadership

[2664] The structure of HG 92/STRAN is essentially geared to addressing national tasks in the context of conventional threats

[2665] The orientation and further development of the structure towards new tasks and capabilities with the resulting requirements (extended national defense within the framework of PSO, ultimately leading to a common defense, subconventional threats, particularly in the form of global terrorism, the battle for information, the threat of long-range air warfare means) is still in the planning phase

[2666] In the medium term, the structural development of the armed forces will therefore be primarily determined by the military-strategic objectives of contributing to conflict prevention and crisis management in an international context, providing assistance in the event of natural disasters and in the context of security police tasks, and maintaining core military capabilities

[2667] The structure of the Federal Army is fundamentally derived from the military strategic objectives resulting from security and defense policy requirements

[2668] Military strategic objectives define the (military) capabilities to be provided, which in turn depend on the probability of occurrence of a threat or operational scenario and on the warning time (time until a conflict becomes effective

[2669] Further determining parameters for the quantitative and qualitative design of the organization are the resources made available by the state

[2670] The structure of the Federal Army is defined in troop divisions

[2671] Currently, a distinction is made between a peace organization and a mob organization

[2672] The following organizational sizes are defined in the ÖBH

[2673] Troop, group, platoon, unit (company, battery, squadron), battalion, squadron, regiment, brigade, division or military command

[2674] Units are formed from the organizational elements squad, group and platoon

[2675] The units are those organizational elements that can independently perform tasks over a short period of time

[2676] Units are grouped into battalions or regiments, which can carry out independent tasks over a period of several days

[2677] Brigades are formed from several battalions and are the command level (organizational size) that ensures combined arms combat (cooperation between the individual branches of the military) and carries out tasks over a longer period of time

[2678] The troop divisions include all the ÖBH departments necessary to fulfil their tasks, from the unit upwards

[2679] In addition to the (previous) distinction between peacetime and mobilization organizations, the Federal Army Reform Commission also distinguishes between the operational organization and the basic organization

[2680] The operational organisation covers those parts of the Federal Army which, within the given force structure, are directly and primarily intended for operations

[2681] The basic organization refers to all those parts of the Federal Army which, within a given force structure, essentially serve to ensure operations while maintaining peacetime operations

[2682] The Austrian Armed Forces are organized into two branches

[2683] The land forces and the air forces

[2684] The main components of the armed forces are the combat troops

[2685] The other branches of the military are represented proportionally in the services

[2686] Land Forces – Overview of Structure and Scope

[2687] The peacetime structure of the Austrian Land Forces consists of a Land Forces Command with two mechanized brigades, three infantry brigades and nine military commands (see Figure

[2688] In terms of troops, the land forces have two signal units, five staff battalions (one per brigade), three reconnaissance battalions, nine Jäger (infantry) battalions, three Panzer battalions, three Panzergrenadier battalions, three Pioneer battalions, two artillery regiments, two Panzer Artillery battalions and (in the area of the Vienna Military Command) the Guard and the Jäger Regiment Vienna

[2689] In addition to their basic infantry skills, some infantry battalions have different specializations such as mountain warfare, air mobility, or different levels of protection and mobility (equipment with armored transport vehicles

[2690] Twenty mobilizable infantry battalions (militia forces) are assigned to the military commands

[2691] Furthermore, the military training areas (Allentsteig, Bruck/Neudorf, Seetaleralpe, Hochfilzen, Ramsau and Lizum) are subordinate to the Land Forces Command, via the respective military commands

[2692] Unlike the armies of other states, the land forces do not have their own army aviation, which is why any air support is provided by the air forces

[2693] Parts of the air force are therefore assigned to the land forces on an ad hoc basis and thus assume the role of the internationally standard army aviation forces

[2779] Readiness is generally the time required to bring a unit or formation (personnel, material, training, etc.) into operational readiness at its peacetime location (home base

[2780] Readiness categories refer to “D-Day” (= Decision Day), the day on which the political decision to deploy troops was made

[2782] KIOP-KPE in the “foreign deployment phase” are on a pre-planned foreign deployment

[2916] Before defining the logistics system for the Austrian Armed Forces, a decision must be made as to whether a logistics task will be solved in-house or whether it can be outsourced to external service providers

[2917] This fundamental question of whether to produce in-house or outsource is a matter of logistics planning and is of strategic importance for every area of logistics

[2918] On the one hand, the trend towards outsourcing services will intensify in peacetime operations in the coming years due to the need to save costs; on the other hand, in the event of a defence situation (due to scarcer military resources), this will lead to a greater reliance on goods from the civilian sector

[2919] In any case, logistical services must be reliable, flexible and, especially in peacetime operations, efficient (economical

[2920] Cost-effectiveness is achieved when, from several methods, the one that causes the lowest total costs for a logistics service is chosen

[2921] The application of cost accounting can provide the decision as to whether logistics services are provided in-house or outsourced

[2922] The use of civilian services reaches its limits where military capabilities are required and legal provisions do not guarantee the enforcement of an agreed service

[2923] In times of extremely tight defense budgets, business management tools and methods (e.g. cost/performance accounting) must be used to identify the most suitable service providers (both internal and external

[2924] The logistics system must primarily meet the requirements of the Austrian Armed Forces in fulfilling its operational tasks

[2925] In a changing range of applications, the sub-areas of the logistics system are constantly subject to critical scrutiny, which leads to changes and adjustments

[2926] Since logistical tasks generally arise from the highest to the lowest management level, but task holders are not available at all levels due to the lack of resources, appropriate management measures and preparations must be taken to ensure sufficient and continuous logistical security in peacetime operations and in operational procedures

[2927] According to the Defence Act, the permanently required organisational facilities (peace organisation) must serve the needs of the organisational framework necessary for operational tasks (operational organisation

[2928] The logistics system must therefore be aligned with this legal requirement and designed in accordance with this fundamental requirement both at the level of central logistics and at the level of troop logistics (a distinction, for example, between peacetime and operational supply is no longer necessary

[2929] The logistics system includes logistics procedures, logistics forces and resources, and logistics organization

[2930] The performance of the logistics system depends, among other things, on the performance of its facilities, the operational readiness of the supply services, the quality and quantity of equipment, the use of civilian resources as well as the command and information systems

[2931] The military leadership must integrate logistics into planning at the military strategic, operational and tactical levels at an early stage

[2932] The contribution of logistics in the command and control process generally consists in situation assessment, planning, command and control

[2933] A logistics information system (LOGIS – see Chapter 7.3.5.4) is part of a management information system and a prerequisite for the planning and control of the logistics sub-areas

[2934] Logistics controlling is an entrepreneurial management concept that focuses on the spatial and temporal structuring of goods movements

[2935] This structuring controls operational processes and influences the costs of operational service provision

[2936] The decisive factor is the appropriate management of the sub-processes with regard to the company's objectives

[2937] Essential goods are understood to be goods and services that are continuously used or consumed (and therefore replenished) or that must be available in a certain (minimum) quantity to maintain operational readiness and combat operations for a certain period of time

[2938] Essential goods are those which the respective association, unit or sub-unit absolutely needs to fulfil the standard task

[2939] When bottlenecks arise, the military leadership must decide who should be supported with priority

[2940] In principle, the “supply principle” applies, i.e. replacement staff, consumables, etc. are brought to the person in need (“bring-on supply”

[2985] Staffing in the logistics sector

[2986] The peacetime organization of the Federal Army provides approximately 15,000 jobs for logistics personnel

[2987] This organizational framework is sufficient to handle national and international tasks, with the exception of medical services

[2988] The organization of the medical service dates back to the time of area defense

[2989] Medical care in peacetime was largely based on contracted army doctors, and the peacetime organization maintained only a small number of medical personnel available for deployment

[2990] Approximately 77% of the jobs for logistics personnel are filled, with occupancy rates of around 80% being reached in the areas of field equipment service, economic service, and territorial logistics

[2991] This compares to a staffing level of around 70% for maintenance personnel, medical personnel, transport personnel and driving personnel

[2992] The lower staffing levels are therefore found in those areas where long specialist training is required, with graduates acquiring a qualification recognized in the civilian sector

[2993] Personnel preparation for deployment Training Training vision

[2994] The training vision, aligned with the military strategic concept, paints a picture of training in the next decade and beyond

[2995] It is incorporated as a supplement to the military strategic concept and, alongside it, forms the basis for the development of the training philosophy

[2996] The structure of the training vision itself is divided into two parts and includes the brief training vision and the associated motivation report

[2997] The motivation report on the training vision highlights the requirements, influencing factors, trends and considerations regarding the development of the armed forces that will determine training in the future

[2998] The conclusions derived from this form the basis for the objectives of the training vision

[2999] Content: The basic command area of training aims to develop armed forces that are well-trained, highly motivated and capable of action, geared to future operational requirements, and that can be deployed both in multinational groups and nationally and are also capable of cooperation with non-military operational organisations

[3000] The training should correspond to modern principles of adult education, be recognized as high-quality in the civil education system and provide prospects for the entire working life

[3001] Through economical training processes and structures, innovation and quality improvement, efficient use of available resources and a focus on operational orientation and interoperability

[3002] Optimised training and training support are intended to enable soldiers and civilian employees to fulfil their tasks most effectively, both in operations and in daily service

[3003] High flexibility, physical fitness, esprit de corps, a sense of values, professionalism at all levels and functions, as well as a high level of reliability in fulfilling missions should shape the image of our soldiers at home and abroad and contribute significantly to a positive image of the Austrian Armed Forces

[3004] Soldiers and civilian employees of the department should make a positive contribution to the positioning of the Austrian Armed Forces in society

[3005] The professional cadre should be enabled to lead multinational armed forces up to the level of large units, to participate in multinational operations across the full spectrum of future operations, including and utilising technological developments, and to cooperate with national operational organisations

[3006] The militia cadre should be brought closer to the qualifications of the professional cadre

[3007] The further development of know-how in the various branches of the military is to be ensured through future-oriented basic work within the school structure

[3008] Synergy effects are to be achieved through international cooperation in training and training support

[3009] The training philosophy is the basic document for the conceptual planning of training in the Austrian Armed Forces

[3010] It is based primarily on the training vision and the military strategic concept and, based on training-relevant derivations, includes well-founded considerations on the training system of the Federal Army and provides guidelines for training and training support

[3011] The training philosophy is supplemented by a motivation report

[3012] The guidelines for training and training support are defined as target specifications in order to allow freedom of action with regard to implementation and subsequently form the basis for the concepts in the training sector

[3013] The educational philosophy is a living matter

[3014] This is expressed in revisions that are either carried out on an ad hoc basis or at periodic intervals

[3015] This ensures that training and training support are always based on current training principles

[3016] Periodic reviews of the training philosophy primarily aim to examine the validity of the content, also in connection with the training vision, and, if necessary, to make appropriate adjustments, the effects of which on the concepts in the training area must be examined and incorporated

[3019] The concepts in the training area form the basis for the further planning and execution or implementation of training and training support as well as their safeguarding

[3020] The training provides soldiers with all the skills needed to ensure the operational readiness of troops and staffs of the Federal Army

[3022] Guidelines for training and training support. Mission statement for training

[3023] Training in the Austrian Armed Forces is operational, future-oriented, and demands and promotes flexibility

[3024] Taking into account lessons learned from operations forms an essential basis for the success of our soldiers in operations

[3025] The training is intended to provide cross-service competence at all levels

[3026] The focus of the training is on both the thoughtful soldier who acts in accordance with the mission and the commander, who, as a commander or technical superior, leads and instructs his subordinates/employees and can set a role model, as well as the independent civilian employee who thinks and acts in accordance with his mission

[3027] Training is appropriate for adults and demanding, using efficient and modern training methods and resources, and is to be carried out with heart, brain, consistency and humor

[3028] It is intended to promote the development of camaraderie, loyalty and trust within the community

[3029] Soldiers, especially professional soldiers, should be able to represent the “Federal Army” in a positive way

[3032] Training, further education and continuing education are a fundamental principle for the promotion of all members of the Austrian Armed Forces

[3033] The establishment of the soldier's operational readiness should demonstrate an efficient relationship between the effort required for training and the use of the function

[3036] They should also be used as a basis for the training, further education and continuing education of civilian employees in an adapted form

[3037] Efficient and effective task performance should be taught and promoted during training in order to ensure subsequent application in the function

[3038] Deputies should receive the same training as commanders

[3039] General aspects of training context

[3040] Training, education and upbringing

[3041] Military training essentially provides the qualifications necessary to exercise the military profession and to perform individual function-specific activities before taking on a specific function

[3042] Consolidation is achieved, among other things, through further training and continuing education

[3043] Training therefore includes not only training measures for professional performance in the narrower sense, but also the transmission of values, thus also aspects of upbringing and education

[3044] These should be taken into account in the planning and implementation of training

[3046] Adult-friendly training and training methods

[3047] The training methods must take operational requirements into account

[3048] The training should be supported and optimized through a balanced use of methods and resources appropriate to the target group, participants and topics, including modern information and communication technology

[3049] Training staff, especially teaching staff at academies and schools, should be given increased training in the use of modern pedagogical tools in the areas of coaching, counselling and support for learners

[3050] Particular attention should be paid to the ability to assess the talents, inclinations and capacities of learners and to provide individual support

[3053] The objectives should be as detailed as necessary, but as general as possible, in order to ensure the flexibility of teaching and learning operations and the freedom of teaching, also in terms of participant orientation

[3055] The willingness and ability of the cadre soldier to practice, train and continuously improve the independent handling of information and knowledge using new media, in addition to organized courses, represents an essential competence in view of current and future requirements for lifelong learning in a knowledge society

[3150] Training by group of people Recruit training

[3151] The aim of basic military service training is to achieve training-related operational readiness of the soldier and the troops up to the unit level

[3152] It is divided into basic training and association training, in which the training of cadre candidates is integrated by way of preparatory cadre training (vbK

[3153] The basic training generally lasts until the end of the fourth month of training

[3154] If basic training is interrupted due to deployment, this training phase will be extended by the length of the interruption

[3155] In this section, the training content that is the same for all soldiers, the weapon- and function-specific (individual) training and the training content of the organizational elements are taught using combat tasks

[3156] The association training lasts until the end of basic military service

[3157] In this section, the organisational elements are to be brought together via training in the sub-unit framework to form units and associations

[3161] The VbK serves to acquire the general and branch-specific basic knowledge required to exercise a cadre/specialist function as a prerequisite for subsequent commander training

[3164] The batch training consists of the batch course (ChK) and further training

[3165] The ChK generally begins six weeks after the end of the main recruitment dates (ET) in January, May or September and lasts 13 to 15 weeks with 65 training days

[3166] The aim of the charge course is to enable the charge to carry out simple commanding duties at squad level, regardless of branch of service, and to represent the group commander at group level – including the implementation of supplies – in peacetime and national operations and as part of a foreign mission

[3300] For 2005/06, the tasks of carrying out peace support operations (PSO) were made the focus of training, both in cadre training and troop training – and thus also in basic military service – and the implementing regulations for basic military service training (DBGWD) were adapted accordingly

[3301] This results in the following training framework being established

[3302] All combat troops must be able to perform peace support missions up to the company level

[3303] All other troops, with the exception of the medical troops, must master the operational tasks up to the platoon level

[3304] All soldiers must receive basic information about the principles and measures of peace support

[3305] Individual aspects of training The shift to the diverse requirements of peace support missions in a multicultural setting requires more than ever before not only trained but also educated soldiers at all command levels

[3306] Every professional, including of course the soldier, belongs to a life world as well as a professional world, which is why education is divided into general education and vocational training

[3307] The fact that the military world can only meaningfully find its significance and classification in the overall political context makes it clear that the education of the soldier, the education of the military, must extend beyond the military sphere

[3308] In this holistic understanding, education should therefore impart to people “purpose-free and coherent knowledge that has grown and is oriented towards intellectual and cultural traditions”

[3309] Education is therefore also concerned with character development and, in addition to knowledge and skills, also includes the aspect of virtue and ethical orientation

[3310] If education fulfills this task, then it also grants a moment of freedom and leads to the ability to actually take on responsibility

[3311] The special responsibility of the soldier and especially of the commander becomes particularly clear when one considers that “hardly any profession is as educationally challenging as that of the soldier, who, in view of the utmost seriousness of military soldierly existence, has to face the existential question of meaning in the face of death, his own as well as that of others.”

[3312] At this point at the latest, it becomes clear that the educated soldier must also have a corresponding world and value orientation

[3313] To date, there is no explicit use or definition of the term education in the regulations of the Austrian Federal Armed Forces

[3314] In the regulation “Military Terms” the terms “advanced training” and “further training” are used around the term “training”

[3315] In contrast, the term education has been used for some time by the German Armed Forces

[3316] “Education is the promotion of the soldier (citizen) in the development of his/her ability to think and judge as well as his/her awareness of values.”

[3317] The new challenges of international security policy and the information and knowledge society place demands on the education of soldiers in a comprehensive sense

[3318] At the commander level, the profile of the new tasks facing the armed forces requires greater competence in social, historical and cultural terms, which will be further promoted by increased civil-military cooperation in security policy, but at the same time also presents educational challenges to political and civilian decision-makers

[3319] Recent efforts underline the recognition of the importance of education as a strategic factor in the Austrian Armed Forces

[3320] For example, the Theresian Military Academy introduced a university of applied sciences diploma course in “Military Leadership,” and the General Staff Course at the National Defence Academy is now offered as an individual diploma course leading to a master’s degree

[3321] In addition to enriching advanced training and continuing education courses with scientific and academic educational content, officer training for troop officers is now offered as a postgraduate course, which concludes with an internationally recognized master's degree in "Masters of Security and Defense Management" for graduates of Leadership Course

[3322] Even if the education of managers should not be made visible solely through the evidence of academic qualifications, it is nevertheless important in today's knowledge and information society to make educational competence recognizable and comparable through these visible academic dimensions

[3323] Not least because the question of the education of officers and non-commissioned officers is of particular importance for the civil-military relationship, the issue of education must be given special attention

[3324] State and military education

[3325] The Federal Army can only adequately fulfill its mandate – military national defense – if its soldiers are willing and able to perform their duties out of conviction

[3326] It is therefore necessary to make all soldiers of the Austrian Armed Forces aware of the need to protect our homeland and its democratic state system and to make the meaning of service with weapons clear and tangible

[3327] Political and defense education encompasses several interconnected areas, such as general political education on the one hand, and defense policy content on the other, concerning comprehensive national defense or the role of the Federal Army in serving the state and society

[3328] It is therefore part of general political education but also part of military training

[3329] The aim is to enable the “military citizen” to recognize the basic values of the democratic order of life in his daily service

[3330] He should be able to recognize and understand the requirements and problems of comprehensive – especially military – national defense in a larger social, political and ethical context

[3331] The awareness of law and duty should be strengthened, as should the awareness of safety and social responsibility

[3332] These contents are taught to conscripts, as well as officers and non-commissioned officers, during their training and are presented in various ways in order to create understanding and to better comprehend connections

[3333] The objectives of state and military education in the Austrian Armed Forces include specific objectives: awareness of democracy and Austria, security awareness, defense awareness, legal and duty awareness, and social awareness

[3334] Implementation takes place as a principle of leadership and service behavior, which means responsible assumption and execution of tasks, combined with mission-oriented leadership and cooperative behavior, as well as creating insight and trust in the meaning of orders or commands

[3335] It also involves special consideration of the human dignity and democratic rights of every soldier in official activities

[3336] Due to the outdated decrees (1980 and 1982) for political education in the Austrian Armed Forces, a new regulation was initiated, which is to be re-enacted in

[3337] In addition to the changed responsibilities and competencies due to interim reorganizations, the new decree will take into account the European dimension in political education in the Federal Armed Forces, particularly in its objectives

[3396] This inevitably led to a certain loss of substance in some areas

[3408] Investment in the financial (business) sense is referred to when it involves measures that change the capacity of the “company” quantitatively and/or qualitatively

[3409] Investment in the narrower sense means the use of financial resources for fixed assets

[3410] The characteristic of fixed assets is that they are available for a large number of performance processes and are not consumed immediately

[3411] The capacity of the “company” is changed quantitatively and/or qualitatively by an investment

[3412] It is irrelevant whether it is a new investment or a replacement or pure reinvestment (e.g. subsequent purchase of motor vehicles

[3413] Accordingly, investment expenditure is broken down as follows: Investment expenditure to improve systems/structures in qualitative and quantitative terms (new acquisitions of fixed assets, upgrading a tactical system from SS to SOPF capabilities, etc

[3414] System/structure maintenance capital expenditures (changes of use, extended inspections, major overhauls, modifications/combat maintenance of fixed assets

[3415] In contrast, all expenditure on circulating goods (consumables) is attributable to ongoing operations

[3416] These are, for example, expenditure on operating resources such as fuels, lubricants, energy, ammunition, raw or auxiliary materials such as material maintenance, excluding expenditure on investments to maintain or improve structures

[3417] In this section, expenditure on non-personnel expenses is examined in more detail, broken down into investments and operating expenses according to the definitions given above

[3476] Mission and objectives

[3477] The basic mandate of the Federal Army Reform Commission (ÖBH 2010) was to develop general principles and framework conditions for adapting the development of military national defense to the threats and challenges at the beginning of the 21st century and to prepare a report on this

[3478] For this purpose, the Federal Minister of Defence established a Federal Army Reform Commission (ÖBH 2010) at the Federal Ministry of Defence (BMLV) pursuant to Section 8, Paragraph 1 of the Federal Ministries Act 1986 (BMG). Its task is to review and further develop the overall and partial strategy, as well as to make recommendations to the Constitutional Convention

[3479] Definition of the scope and effectiveness of Austria's military contribution to international crisis management with particular consideration of the ESDP, including aspects of the Euro-Atlantic security structure

[3480] further considerations in the sense of a common European defence

[3481] Continuation of the redimensioning of the leadership and administrative structures in the National Defence Department based on the results of REORG

[3482] The Federal Army Reform Commission had the following objectives: Development of the basis for the reform

[3483] Clarification of all questions relating to the military safeguarding of Austrian sovereignty

[3484] • Consideration of the following additional requirements

[3485] Implementation of the recommendations of the security and defence doctrine, including • Ensuring the necessary personnel levels by creating the necessary framework

[3486] Preparation of a contribution to a national CIMIC concept

[3487] The starting point for the establishment of the reform commission was the statement in the government program of the Austrian federal government for the XXII

[3488] legislative period that “external security and military national defense are essential and indispensable elements for ensuring peace, freedom, security and stability for Austria and its citizens,” and that the Federal Government will therefore do everything in its power to “further increase the effectiveness of the Federal Army and strengthen its status in society.”

[3489] Due to its objective, the work of the Federal Army Reform Commission was particularly focused on creating the foundations for a comprehensive, long-term and sustainable reform of the Austrian Armed Forces in the sense of a future project ÖBH. The essential basis for the work of the commission was the draft of the partial strategy for defense policy developed by the Federal Ministry of Defense in accordance with the security and defense doctrine

[3490] This report compiles and analyses the current facts, derives the expected challenges for Austrian defence policy for the period 2010/2015 and forms the basis for the formation of needs-based armed forces within the framework of a comprehensive and sustainable reform of the Austrian Armed Forces

[3501] Austrian Armed Forces Reform

[3502] Following the submission of the report of the Federal Army Reform Commission on 14 June 2004, the Federal Minister of Defence commissioned the Chief of the General Staff to establish a project organisation under the working title Management ÖBH 2010 (Mng ÖBH

[3503] The preparatory work for this was completed as per the contract in mid-July 2004, so that the development of an initial target structure for the Federal Army, including deployment planning, framework conditions and drafts of the legal basis necessary for implementation, could begin

[3506] The starting point for the first processing phase of the Mgmt ÖBH 2010 was a working hypothesis based on the recommendations of the Federal Army Reform Commission

[3507] Other basic documents are the security and defense doctrine and the draft defense policy sub-strategy

[3508] The end of the East-West conflict and the expansion of the European Union and NATO have fundamentally changed the security policy framework for Austria

[3509] There is no conventional military threat to Austrian territory in the foreseeable future

[3510] However, the effects of European and non-European instabilities as well as subconventional threats may continue to influence Austria's security in the future

[3511] A permanent strategic assessment and evaluation of the situation is therefore essential

[3512] Forces intended exclusively for the defense of Austrian territory against conventional threats are therefore no longer required in the presence structure of the Austrian Armed Forces to the same extent as before

[3513] For the Austrian Armed Forces, this means that in the future, when carrying out its domestic tasks, it must fundamentally and primarily concentrate on maintaining state sovereignty and providing assistance

[3514] As a member of the European Union, Austria is increasingly integrated into the structures of European crisis management

[3515] Likewise, new threats can only be addressed in the international communities and the European Union through increased international cooperation

[3516] Without a safe environment, there can be no safe Austria

[3517] It is therefore in Austria’s security policy interest to participate in the European Security and Defence Policy

[3518] Of course, Austria will also have to make an appropriate military and civilian contribution

[3519] For the Austrian Armed Forces, this means that the ability to participate in demanding European crisis management missions, as defined on the one hand by the expanded spectrum of Petersberg tasks and on the other hand by possible further developments, is the determining factor for the development of its capacities to perform international tasks

[3562] The Federal Army

[3563] The tasks of the Federal Army within the country are: - the maintenance of state sovereignty on the ground and in the air, - the military protection of the population and their livelihoods, - disaster protection

[3564] To achieve this, at least 10,000 soldiers must be permanently available at home

[3565] Austria’s security is inextricably linked to European security

[3566] Therefore, the Austrian Armed Forces (ÖBH) increasingly have to fulfil the following tasks abroad: Military conflict prevention and crisis management within the framework of the UN, NATO/PfP, the OSCE and in particular EU missions across the entire spectrum of Petersberg tasks, including participation in EU battlegroups, humanitarian aid, disaster relief operations

[3567] The Austrian Armed Forces will have the capacity to permanently deploy up to 1,500 soldiers abroad or, in the medium term, to provide a framework brigade of up to 3,500 soldiers for one year

[3568] In the future, newly assigned personnel will have to undertake overseas deployments

[3569] Austrian Armed Forces 2010 – Structure

[3570] The structure of the Austrian Armed Forces will be as follows: - a total strength of 55,000 soldiers; - a Joint Forces Command, to which all elements of the land forces (brigades, military commands, the foreign operations base, the command support units, an information operations element, the CIMIC element), all elements of the air force, and the special operations forces will be subordinate

[3571] The Armed Forces Command is responsible for the command of all Austrian Armed Forces operations at home and abroad

[3572] This means that the preparation and execution of an operation (land and air forces, national and international operations) are all under one roof

[3573] This means administrative simplification, shortening and accelerating official channels, as well as personnel and organizational savings in the administration

[3574] ¾ an operational support command, which is responsible for the logistical support of the entire Austrian Armed Forces, including the central office and the medical services

[3575] The troop structure includes elements of the land forces as well as four brigades that are to be completely restructured

[3576] This leads to staff concentration and greater professionalization

[3577] Within these brigades, cadre-present elements are formed that can be deployed at any time as a well-coordinated team at home and abroad

[3578] The number of battalions is reduced from 36 to

[3579] The force structure also includes the Air Force (the small units of the Air Force will be reduced from 20 to 12) with air surveillance (radar elements, air surveillance aircraft and air defence) and air support (air transport and reconnaissance) as well as the Special Operations Forces, which will assume an even more important role in the future for special tasks to protect Austrian citizens and soldiers abroad (e.g. evacuation operations) and will have an increased number of personnel

[3580] The militia continues to be an indispensable part of the Austrian Armed Forces

[3581] The militiamen are generally used as an integral part of the present units in all functions, for the formation of independent militia battalions and units, as well as in the expert pools

[3582] The new structure requires efficient locations

[3583] Properties no longer required are sold

[3584] During the conceptual design phase, the utility value of the existing locations was determined using a scientific method

[3585] The Federal Army Reform Commission has already recommended selling up to 40% of the Federal Army’s real estate

[3586] % of the proceeds from the sale will go towards the reform

[3587] The military commands remain the territorial superior commands of all units stationed in the state and assume the following important tasks

[3588] Contact person for the state and the population, liaison office for the population and all federal agencies in the states and state departments, representative of the interests of the Austrian Armed Forces in the states, public relations and contact and coordination point in the event of a disaster

[3589] A reduction in military commands of up to 40 percent is planned

[3590] Austrian Armed Forces 2010 – Personnel

[3591] Basic military service will last six months starting January

[3592] There will be a general reorientation of the training content

[3593] The aim is to ensure that recruits are able to be deployed on a graduated basis for general and specific assistance missions

[3594] Early branch-specific training should form the basis for all possible subsequent assignments (junior cadre recruits, junior cadre recruits, overseas service, militia assignments

[3595] The continuation of the assistance mission to protect the border in accordance with the Schengen Agreement in Lower Austria and Burgenland must be ensured

[3596] The aim is to achieve a 1:1 ratio between troops and basic organization in terms of personnel

[3597] This makes it necessary to reallocate positions for soldiers from the basic organization to the troops

[3598] This requires changes in service, salary and pension law as well as incentive systems to increase mobility

[3599] Austrian Armed Forces 2010 – Financing Initial funding is required to implement the reform

[3600] The key factors for the success of the reform are therefore: - the rapid availability of funds released through the reduction of operating expenses, - rapid realisation of property revenues, - an appropriately measured and constant share of the defence budget in GDP

[3615] European Security and Defence Policy (ESDP

[3616] The Commission considers that the ESDP is developing as an instrument of the Common Foreign and Security Policy (CFSP) for conflict prevention and crisis management, is intended to strengthen Europe's autonomy in security policy and excludes any use and presence of weapons of mass destruction

[3617] On this basis and in line with the existing decisions within the EU with regard to the CFSP and ESDP, which Austria fully supports within the current constitutional situation (in particular the Federal Constitutional Law on Neutrality, Article 23f of the Federal Constitutional Law, the CFE-BVG), the Commission recommends: the creation of the conditions for Austria’s military participation in multinational conflict prevention and crisis management operations, with the international tasks of the Federal Armed Forces being determined by participation in UN or OSCE-mandated missions and in the increasingly demanding EU crisis management missions

[3618] These are defined in their entirety by the Petersberg Tasks

[3619] Possible further developments in the ESDP, for example in the context of a future EU constitution, would have to be taken into account on the basis of a broad political consensus

[3620] to take steps in this context to enable Austria to participate in any assistance provided on the basis of the European Council Declaration of 25 March 2004 on ‘Solidarity against Terrorism’

[3621] ¾ the necessary resources for an appropriate Austrian participation in the “EU

[3622] Headline Goal (e.g. “Helsinki Force Catalogue”

[3623] ¾ ensuring access to information relevant to armaments policy and the ongoing assessment of possible participation in European armaments projects

[3624] Close cooperation with European partners for the purpose of coordinating multinational units (e.g. within the framework of the EU Battlegroups Concept) and operations

[3625] Taking national interests into account, preference should be given to regional cooperation and collaboration with regional partners

[3626] appropriate participation by Austria in all permanent or ad hoc military command structures established or used by the EU, as well as ensuring military advice for Austrian representatives in the EU's political and diplomatic decision-making bodies

[3627] In addition, the Commission recommends: strengthening existing approaches to whole-of-government coordination and development of security and defence policy through instruments such as the National Security Council (NSC) or processes for updating a strategic situational picture

[3628] the most flexible possible design of military contributions to international crisis management, so that the political leadership always has at its disposal an instrument adapted to Austria's objectives and possibilities

[3629] Close cooperation with NATO within the framework of the Partnership for Peace (PfP) in the interest of establishing the interoperability of the Austrian Armed Forces in order to achieve the standards that are a prerequisite for participation in UN or OSCE-mandated missions and in EU crisis management

[3637] to assign the Federal Army an important role in protecting the vital, civilian information and communication technology (ICT) infrastructure and in maintaining redundant systems in the event of a disaster or threat, both within the framework of security police assistance operations and within the framework of state crisis management
